name: Citrine Informatics, Inc.
subcategory: materials informatics SaaS (AI for materials and chemicals R&D)
origin_detail: Founded 2013 by Greg Mulholland (CEO) and Bryce Meredig, both Stanford Graduate School of Business graduates, to combine materials data infrastructure with AI. HQ Redwood City, CA; Pittsburgh office (2017), Tokyo office (2020).
flagship_projects: Catalyst natural-language assistant (Oct 2023; relaunched with Apex Jul 2026)
openness_notes: The platform is proprietary enterprise SaaS. Peripheral pieces are open under Apache-2.0 on GitHub: citrine-python (SDK), gemd-python (GEMD data model), lolo (random-forest ML library, ~53 stars) and dft-input-gen. The older python-citrination-client and public_search repositories are archived. Level 1: SDKs, data model and a library are open; the product is closed. A first-hand description of the former Citrination data service was not available in fetched sources.

license_history.license: Proprietary Citrine Platform; Apache-2.0 citrine-python, gemd-python, lolo

risk_events: Small rounds by 2025-2026 standards: $7.6M (Jun 2017), $8M convertible note (Apr 2018), $20M Series B (Oct 2019), strategic investments from Universal Materials Incubator (Dec 2020) and Evonik Venture Capital (Mar 2022, amounts undisclosed), $16M Series C (Jan 2023)
No announced equity round since Jan 2023 through Nov 2026; non-dilutive awards (DOE $3.1M 2022, ARPA-E $0.3M 2024, DARPA INTACT 2025, BioMADE 2026)
2026: repositioned around generative AI (Apex, 'Industrial Super Intelligence') as better-funded AI-for-materials entrants arrived
robustness: A long-lived (13 years) independent SaaS with blue-chip chemical and materials customers (LyondellBasell, Eastman, Evonik, Huntsman, Arkema, Saint-Gobain, TotalEnergies, Syensqo and others) and government-funded projects. Capital-light compared with 2025 entrants. The platform is proprietary, but the open GEMD data model and Apache SDKs reduce lock-in.
physical_science_relevance: Very high. AI for materials and chemicals formulation: polymers and urethanes (LANXESS), glass (AGC), batteries (Morrow, Sion Power), CO2-based polymers (Econic), coatings (Dorfner, Perstorp), nuclear-waste storage materials (DOE), fusion (ARPA-E), bio-produced cement (BioMADE) and mineral processing (ANZAPLAN).
openness_effect_assessment: Citrine's revenue comes from closed enterprise SaaS for chemical companies whose private, sparse datasets they will not share. Its open pieces (GEMD data model, lolo, SDKs) lower integration costs and support academic credibility but were never the business. The archived Citrination-era client repositories suggest the company's open public-data face has receded as enterprise SaaS grew.
key_takeaway: Citrine is the incumbent US materials-informatics startup, founded in 2013. It shows the slow, capital-light path: about $52M or more in announced rounds over a decade, real industrial customers and grants, and peripheral open tooling (Apache-2.0 SDK, data model, ML library) around a closed SaaS core. By 2025-2026 it was dwarfed in funding by closed AI-for-materials newcomers (Periodic Labs' $300M seed, CuspAI's >$650M), and responded by rebranding around 'industrial superintelligence' rather than opening up.

unconfirmed.reason: No page states a total. Each announced component is confirmed by its own release, separate from the cited listing page: '$7.6 million Series A' (7 Jun 2017), '$8 million convertible note from Tencent Holdings' (19 Apr 2018), $20M Series B (10 Oct 2019), '$16 million Series C' (4 Jan 2023). SEC Form Ds suggest the $51.6M sum is understated: equity sold was $8,757,049 (first sale 2016-05-09), $20,948,322 (2019-06-28), $12,354,375 (2020-10-23, possibly the undisclosed Dec 2020 UMI investment) and $12,595,504 (2022-10-28, partial Series C). That is $54.7M through 2022 (my arithmetic) before the $8M note. Whether the 2016 Form D overlaps the 2017 Series A is not stated. No single page contradicts $51.6M, so it was not changed.

newer_info.evidence: Increment, not a cumulative total: Form D new notice, equity, date of first sale 2023-09-15, total amount sold 4999999
Increment, not a cumulative total: Form D new notice, equity/options, date of first sale 2025-01-24, offering 6100000, amount sold 2604987

verification_pass2.note: founded_year is now independently confirmed by an SEC filing. risk_events[1] ('No announced equity round since Jan 2023') is true only for announcements: Form Ds show unannounced equity sales in Sep 2023 ($5.0M) and Jan 2025 ($2.6M). Minor date drift: the listing page dates the Series C to 23 Jan 2023, but the release itself is dated 4 Jan 2023. Confidence was not raised to high because the funding total is unconfirmed and probably understated.
